relationships.subject: Morphine
relationships.evidence_quote: Morphine and oxycodone at 0.1 μM to 100 μM dose-dependently increased endothelial cell tube formation and proliferation.

relationships.evidence_quote: Morphine and fentanyl at 1, 10 and 100 μM significantly decreased pro-apoptotic protein Bax without affecting Bcl-2 level (Fig. 5A and B).

relationships.evidence_quote: Morphine and fentanyl at 1, 10 and 100 μM significantly decreased pro-apoptotic protein Bax without affecting Bcl-2 level (Fig. 5A and B).

relationships.evidence_quote: We found that morphine, fentanyl and oxycodone at 0.1 μM, 1 μM and 10 μM increased p-p44/42 MAPK without affecting level of total MAPK

relationships.subject: PD98059
relationships.evidence_quote: We found that PD98059 blocked morphine-induced endothelial cell tube formation, growth and survival (Fig. 7C to E).

relationships.subject: Naloxone
relationships.evidence_quote: We found that naloxone did not antagonize morphine, fentanyl or oxycodone-induced capillary network formation (Fig. 6A) or endothelial cell growth (Fig. 6B).

relationships.subject: VEGF
relationships.evidence_quote: we demonstrated that VEGF increased HUVEC tube formation by ~ 2.5 fold compared with control

key_findings: Morphine, fentanyl and oxycodone but not codeine promoted endothelial tube formation and proliferation, independent of mu-opioid receptor (naloxone-insensitive).
Only morphine acted via MAPK activation (reversed by PD98059); fentanyl and oxycodone used other mechanisms.
